correctness.rationale: An exhaustive four-class partition decomposes the exact finite partition function. Uniform fixed-parameter logarithmic expansions and concentration of conditional binomial counts prove the three-atom weak limit. The derivative of e^{-c^2}cosh(kappa c) and monotonicity of tanh(t)/t prove the sharp kappa=sqrt(2) threshold and unique positive stationary point when kappa>sqrt(2). Exact rational enumeration reproduced 64 finite cases and independent stable numerical checks tested the limit and derivative behavior; these support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the explicitly scaled three-atom occupation law and sharp two-species reentrance threshold kappa=sqrt(2) on nearly balanced complete bipartite graphs. This is not the known exact finite partition count, regular-graph extremal bound, infinite-tree Gibbs reentrance, or square/Bethe lattice multicomponent phase diagram. Exact graph-counting representations are acknowledged as covering the finite partition identity; no examined scientific statement includes the particular n^{-1/2} activity and n^{1/2} imbalance joint scaling or its nonmonotone two-part occupancy event. That is an examined-evidence originality judgment, not a uniqueness guarantee.

value.rationale: The complete bipartite family is a natural mean-field/dense-graph benchmark for hard-exclusion two-species gases. The joint square-root imbalance and activity window identifies three sharply separated occupation patterns with an exact crossover function, yet the total occupation scale alone cannot distinguish them. A sharp imbalance threshold produces reentrant probability of simultaneous occupation of both parts even with just two species and strict repulsion. This is a structural boundary for an interpretable event, not a numerical table, arbitrary slice, or claim of true infinite-volume symmetry breaking.
